title: window.open('chrome-extension://…') từ web page → chrome-error://chromewebdata/ — phải route qua SW chrome.tabs.create
trigger: Bất kỳ click handler nào trong content script / shadow-DOM popup mở một extension page (popup, options, reconnect flow)
principle: Web pages are not allowed to navigate to chrome-extension:// URLs — window.open(getURL(...)) resolves to chrome-error://chromewebdata/ silently, no console error. Extension-initiated navigation works: content script sendMessage → service worker chrome.tabs.create({ url: chrome.runtime.getURL(path) }). Same rule applies to location.assign/href. When the opened page must heal state (file-handle re-grant), attach capture-phase pointerdown/keydown listeners that call the heal helper — the user's first click on the page supplies the transient activation requestPermission needs. Note: requestPermission on a handle whose grant never persisted (e.g. CDP drop-grant) shows the real native 'Allow this site to view…' prompt — approvable in E2E only via OS-level automation (UIAutomation Invoke on the Allow button), while picker-granted handles re-grant silently.

cases.context: Dictionary popup local-audio reconnect hint rendered a button doing window.open(chrome.runtime.getURL('popup/index.html')). Real-browser E2E: click opened chrome-error://chromewebdata/ and permission stayed 'prompt'.
cases.good:
void sendMessage({ type: 'LOCAL_AUDIO_OPEN_RECONNECT', payload: {} });
// SW handler: await chrome.tabs.create({ url: chrome.runtime.getURL('src/entrypoints/popup/index.html') });

applyFor: Any UX that deep-links a web page into an extension surface (reconnect, settings, onboarding)
Reviewers: flag any window.open/location assignment to chrome.runtime.getURL() in content-script code
E2E on permission flows: expect a native file-access prompt for never-durably-granted handles; approve via UIAutomation or pre-grant via picker semantics
